# Usage Examples

One harness engine, three surfaces: the terminal UI, the Python API, and the web UI.
Same tools, same slash vocabulary, same task lifecycle.

## 1. Terminal UI

```bash
python -m berg_agents --tui
```

Bare text runs a `generic` task; `/harness` (alias `/task`) runs it with an explicit harness task type:

```
harness> refactor the login flow to use sessions
harness> /harness add retry logic to the sync worker
harness> /agents
harness> /stats
harness> /help
```

### Slash commands (identical list and order in the web picker)

  | Command             | What it does                   |
  | ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
  | `/help`             | Show all slash commands        |
  | `/agents`           | List registered agents         |
  | `/models`           | Show available models (web UI) |
  | `/stats`            | Learning statistics            |
  | `/tools`            | List available tools (web UI)  |
  | `/health`           | System health check (web UI)   |
  | `/history`          | Show session task transcript   |
  | `/memory`           | Memory information (web UI)    |
  | `/context`          | Show current context (web UI)  |
  | `/settings`         | Show settings (web UI)         |
  | `/plugins`          | List plugins (web UI)          |
  | `/skills`           | List skills (web UI)           |
  | `/mcps`             | MCP server status (web UI)     |
  | `/harness`, `/task` | Run a task through the harness |
  | `/clear`            | Clear the session              |

Commands marked "web UI" are listed in the TUI for parity but answered there with a web-only notice.
Unknown commands warn and continue --- they never kill the session.

## 2. Python API

```python
from berg_agents.app import BergAgentsApp

app = BergAgentsApp.create()
# app.harness, app.agent, app.workspace, app.loop
# app.serve(host="0.0.0.0", port=8001)  # serve explicitly
```

`create()` assembles objects from the resolved config; it starts no server.
Call `.serve(...)` to expose the API.
Entry flags live in `berg_agents/__main__.py`: `--tui` / `--cli` for the terminal, otherwise web with `--host` / `--port` (defaults `0.0.0.0:8001`).

## 3. Web UI

```bash
# Build the static UI once (FastAPI serves the export on the same origin)
cd berg_agents/ui/webapp && npm install && npm run build

python -m berg_agents --web --port 8001
# → http://127.0.0.1:8001
```

Type `/` for the slash-command picker (same commands as the TUI).
Agent, HITL, and learning panels follow the same task lifecycle the TUI renders.
Session search and restore live at `/history`.

### Frontend development loop

```bash
python -m berg_agents --web --port 8001   # backend API
cd berg_agents/ui/webapp && NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8001 npm run dev
# → http://localhost:3000 (3001 if taken)
```

The dev server is cross-origin, so it needs the backend URL at startup (inlined by Next.js) --- without it all `/api/*` calls 404 against Next.js itself.
The backend allows CORS from `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` on ports 3000--3001 only.
Production needs none of this: one origin serves API plus static build.

### Plugin surfaces

Toolbar buttons are generated from `GET /api/plugins` --- one per plugin declaring a `ui:` block, using its `label`.
The host runtime-imports the plugin's built bundle once (cached by URL) and mounts the named export with `PluginSurfaceProps` (`view`, `refreshKey`, `onClose`, `onToggleView`, `onCount`, ...).
`refreshKey` bumps when that plugin's tool completes in the transcript, so the panel reflects what the agent just did without polling.
Bundles are served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so rebuilds appear on next navigation.
Failures render an explicit reason --- never a blank panel.
Full contract: [Plugin UI](plugins/PLUGIN-UI.qmd); pilot: [Shared-ToDo](plugins/SHARED-TODO.qmd).

## 4. Calling tools directly

Synchronous single-tool execution (what a slash-typed `/read_file x` calls):

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/tool/execute \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "tool": "read_file", "args": { "file_path": "README.md" } }'
```

`args` may also be a bare string (treated as `file_path`).
`run_task` is special-cased to run the full harness pipeline.
Failures return `status: "error"` output --- never tracebacks.
Tool names and risk classes: `GET /api/tools`.

Plugin tools go through one generic shape:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/plugins/berg-plugin-shared-todo/tools/list_todo_items \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

Unknown plugin or tool returns 404.
Nothing todo-specific remains in host routes.

## 5. Human-in-the-loop

Tool risk classes (`berg_agents/agents/factory.py`) decide the pause: `low` (`list_files`, `read_file`, `search_code`, `plan_task`) runs unattended; `high` (`bash`, `edit_file`, `patch_file`, `write_file`, `implement_task`, sensitive MCP) pauses.

- **TUI**: the result panel shows review reasons, then `Approve and resume? [y/N]:` --- approval re-executes with `hitl_decision: approve` in metadata, anything else fails the task as rejected.
- **Web**: the HITL surface shows tool name plus arguments with Approve / Reject / Edit (edit rewrites the args before the tool runs).
- **Read-only / no-shell deployments** withhold mutating tools at registration --- stronger than asking the model not to use them.
- Failed sends auto-reject orphaned approvals with a retry-friendly reason plus a dismissible alert; orphaned approval ids from dead runs are stripped on restore and marked expired, never replayed.

## 6. Sessions, memory, compaction in daily use

- Sessions persist as full `Conversation` JSON in `{config}/chat_sessions.db` (`GET` / `POST` / `PATCH` / `DELETE /api/sessions…`); a server-side `active_session` pointer (`GET` / `POST /api/sessions/current`, set on create/send/restore) keeps fresh tabs converging instead of minting duplicates.
- Memory: `write_memory` files durable facts to `{config}/memory/MEMORY.md`; a bounded snapshot is injected beside every user message, refreshed each request.
  `read_memory` / `search_memory` are for topic files only --- never re-read `MEMORY.md` itself.
  Details: [Memory & Compaction](MEMORY.qmd).
- Compaction (`TieredCompaction`: dedupe reads, then clear old tool results, then clamp oversized parts, then summarize once, receipts on) runs before the memory block is attached; `ReportContextUsage` feeds the live context gauge.
  `StepPersistence` plus `ConversationSearch` keep compacted-away turns recallable by keyword.
- Plugin enable/disable (`POST /api/plugins/{id}/enable|disable`) applies on the next chat turn.
  Config `enabled: false` is the startup kill-switch default; runtime state is authoritative after that.
